[[Elizabeth, New Jersey]] }} '''Kyrie Andrew Irving''' (born March 23, 1992) is an [[Australian American]] [[college basketball]] player for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University]] [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils men's basketball team]]. He was one of the top-rated high school basketball players in the United States in the class of 2010. ==High school career== Irving played for [[Montclair Kimberley Academy]] his freshman and sophomore year, where he averaged 26.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 3.6 steals and became only the school's second 1,000 point scorer, before transferring to St. Patrick's.{{cite web|author=Adam ZagoriaSpecial to Rivals High |url=http://highschool.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=902176 |title=Rivals High - Kyrie Irving ready to return after wait period |publisher=Highschool.rivals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}} Irving was the #2 player in the class of 2010 by [[Scout.com]],{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2010 |title=Scout.com: Football Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}} #3 player in the [[ESPNU]] 100,{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/tracker/espnu100?&season=2010&action=upsell&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fncb%2frecruiting%2ftracker%2fespnu100%3f%26season%3d2010 |title=College Basketball Recruiting - ESPNU 100 - ESPN |publisher=Insider.espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}} and rated as the #4 player by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1909 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for class of 2010 |publisher=Rivalshoops.rivals.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}} While at [[St. Patrick's High School (New Jersey)|St. Patrick's High School]], Irving played with [[Michael Gilchrist]], who is widely regarded as the one of the best players in the class of 2011.{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2288 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking - Rivals150 for the class of 2011 |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}}{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2011 |title=Scout.com: Men's Basketball Recruiting |publisher=Scouthoops.scout.com |date= |accessdate=2010-08-26}} On January 20, 2010, it was announced that Irving was selected to the 2010 Junior National Select Team. The team played at the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] at the [[Rose Garden (arena)|Rose Garden]] in [[Portland, Oregon]], on April 10.{{cite web|last=|first=url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2010/01/its-the-usa-against-everyone-else/ |title=It’s the USA Against Everyone Else |publisher=Slam Online |date=2010-01-20 |accessdate=2010-08-26}} He was also selected to play in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]]{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204886340 |title=Kyrie Irving Selected For McDonald’s All-American Game - Duke University Blue Devils | Official Athletics Site |publisher=GoDuke.com |date=2010-07-01 |accessdate=2010-08-26}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kyrie Irving | position = [[Point Guard|PG]] | hometown = West Orange, New Jersey | highschool = St. Patrick HS | feet = 6 | inches = 2 | weight = 175 | 40 = | commitdate = October 22, 2009 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2010 | rivals ref title = Duke Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = 2010 Duke Basketball Commits | espn ref title = ESPN | rivals school = 2 | scout s = 167 | espn school id = 150 | scout overall = 2 | rivals overall = 4 | espn overall = 3 | accessdate = 2011-01-21 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Irving committed to [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] on October 22, 2009, in a television broadcast on [[ESPNU]]. Irving started playing with Duke in the [[2010-11 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010–11 basketball season]] under the guidance of head coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]]. He led the team in scoring at 17.4 points per game on 53.2% shooting through the first eight games of the season. In addition, he added 5.1 assists, 3.8 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game as he quickly began to make his case for NCAA Freshman of the Year. In Duke's 8th game of the season, Irving suffered a severe ligament injury in his right big toe that sidelined him indefinitely. His right foot was placed in a cast on December 10, 2010. The cast was removed on February 4, 2011, and Irving began rehab. On March 17, the day before Duke played Hampton in the first round of the NCAA tournament, it was revealed that Kyrie would return for his first game since Dec. 4th. It was announced that he would come off of the bench and play limited minutes. Duke lost to Arizona in the Sweet Sixteen. Irving scored 28 points in what turned out to be his last game for Duke. {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | [[2010-11 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2010–11]] | align="left" | [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] | 11 || 11 || 29.8 || .529 || .462 || .901 || 3.4 || 4.3 || 1.5 || 0.5 || 20.5 |- | align="left" | Career | align="left" | | 11 || 11 || 29.8 || .529 || .462 || .901 || 3.4 || 4.3 || 1.5 || 0.5 || 20.5 {{S-end}} ==Professional career== Irving announced that he would forgo his final three seasons of eligibility and enter the [[2011 NBA Draft]] where he is the consensus choice to be selected as the number 1 pick. He signed an agent in early May 2011.{{cite web|last= |first= |title=Kyrie Irving entering NBA draft |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2011/news/story?id=6301656 |work=ESPN.com |date=April 6, 2011 |accessdate=}} ==Personal life== Irving was born in [[Melbourne]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], [[Australia]] where his father, Drederick Irving, played professional basketball for the [[Bulleen Boomers]]. Irving subsequently lived in Australia before relocating to the United States at the age of 2. He has dual citizenship in the United States and Australia{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/u18/10_mu18_q_a_irving.html |title=Kyrie Irving is Committed to the Red, White and Blue |publisher=USA Basketball |date=2010-06-21 |accessdate=2010-08-26}} and has recently expressed interest in representing the [[Australia national basketball team|Australian National Team]].{{cite web|url=http://blogs.fayobserver.com/accbasketball/May-2011/Kyrie-Irving-%E2%80%98seriously-considering%E2%80%99-playing-for-A |title=Kyrie Irving ‘seriously considering’ playing for Australian national team|publisher=Fay Observer |date=2011-05-20 |accessdate=2011-05-22}} Irving's mother, Elizabeth, died from an illness when he was four, so his father Drederick raised him with the help of Kyrie's aunts.[http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news;_ylt=ApgBBmFAvYXWRtcZVki58OK8vLYF?slug=mc-spears_kyrie_irving_father_nba_draft_061711 Irving rewards father's perseverance] on ''[[Yahoo!]]'' Sports;
